problem:
The displacement $s$ (in meters) relative to a fixed origin $O$ of a particle moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis is given by the equation $s(t)={3}^{3t+1}$, where $t$ is the time, measured in seconds. Find the position ${s}_{0}$ and velocity ${v}_{0}$ of the particle at the initial moment of time $t=0\,\text{s}.$

${s}_{0}=$
{{field-1}}$\text{m}\,\text{and}\,$

${v}_{0}=$
{{field-2}}$\text{m/s}$
worked_solution:
To calculate the initial position, we substitute $t=0$ it into the equation $s(t)={3}^{3t+1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}_{0} & =s(0) \\  & ={3}^{3(0)+1} \\  & =3\,\text{m}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({3}^{3t+1}) \\  & =3\cdot {3}^{3t+1}\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\  & ={3}^{3t+2}\operatorname{ln}⁡3\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the velocity at $t=0\,\text{s},$ we substitute $t=0$ into the velocity function above:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{0} & =v(0) \\  & ={3}^{3(0)+2}\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\  & =9\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$
